title: Every Little Letter
style: Children’s rock, uplifting, bright live-band groove with punchy kick and snare, bouncing bass, crunchy friendly electric-guitar chords, and handclap accents. Start with a playful guitar-and-clap intro, build through story-led verses, then open into a big easy-to-sing chorus with group backing vocals; add a short guitar-and-keys lift before the final chorus. Clear youthful lead vocal, warm harmonies, lively but uncluttered family-friendly mix.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
First day, nineteen seventy-seven
Wooden plane tucked in my hand
Three little planes, four little claimants
I was the one who couldn’t land
But on my page, I made a start
One small word I knew by heart

[Pre-Chorus]
A-vión, I wrote it down
Letters ready, feet on the ground

[Chorus]
Eme, eme, that’s the name I knew
Syllable by syllable, we read it through
Luz Elena right beside me
Two young voices, one big key
Sapo, not rana, there on page seven
Words opened up like a door to heaven
Eme, eme, say it with me
Every little letter set us free

[Verse 2]
Nineteen seventy-eight, Federman
Grandma Ana’s house behind
José Max León, a brand-new classroom
A reading book we opened side by side
Sixteen months between our birthdays
Still we sounded every part
Letters clicked and words came walking
Like a map drawn in the heart

[Pre-Chorus]
Teacher said “mmm,” I thought, “I see—
That’s for the others, not for me!”

[Chorus]
Eme, eme, that’s the name I knew
Syllable by syllable, we read it through
Luz Elena right beside me
Two young voices, one big key
Sapo, not rana, there on page seven
Words opened up like a door to heaven
Eme, eme, say it with me
Every little letter set us free

[Bridge]
Three planes, four hands, one left out
Then letters turned the whole thing round
I could name the sounds, the words, the page
A little reader taking center stage

[Final Chorus]
Eme, eme, that’s the name I knew
Syllable by syllable, we read it through
Luz Elena right beside me
Two young voices, one big key
Sapo, not rana, clear as can be
The label told the truth to me
Eme, eme, say it with me
Every little letter set us free

[Outro]
Avión, sapo, words I could see
Eme, eme—read along with me!
